examples.pie: kʷíd sruméni nigʷtóm h₁ésti? pĺ̥h₂seh₂ nigʷtéh₂ h₁ésti.

examples.pie: nigʷtéh₂ yéwgos pértum h₂éǵet wr̥ǵyét-kʷe.

root.gloss: to crack, crush (foodstuff), pulverize (grain); to cook; to ripen

examples.pie: déh₃tōr pkʷtrés méǵh₂yōs h₁ést pékʷtōr-kʷe méd méǵh₂yōs h₁ést.
examples.en: The giver was greater than the cook, and the cook was greater than I.

examples.pie: dh₃trés népōts pékʷtōr bʰúHt pékʷet-kʷe só dʰoHnéh₂m.
examples.en: The giver's grandson became a cook, and he cooked the grain.

examples.pie: gʰóstey túH priHós. nu pékʷtōr h₁édnom h₂réydʰet. puHróm wósh₂r̥-kʷe h₁ddʰí pl̥h₁dʰí-kʷe.
examples.en: Guest, you are dear! The cook prepared the food. Eat the grain and the garlic, and be full!

root.gloss: to fart loudly, pass gas, break wind

examples.pie: kʷís pótey pérdt? pótni ḱwṓ pérdt. h₂éǵroy h₂éwibʰis ḱóm h₁ésti. nu h₂éǵrōd pérdetor. só méǵh₂s ḱwṓ. túH méǵh₂s ḱwṓ.
examples.en: Husband, who farted? The dog farted, wife. He is in the field with the sheep. Then he farts from the field. He is a great dog! You are the great dog.

examples.pie: ǵr̥h₂n̥tés ǵn̥h₁yóh₂er. stéh₃mn̥ moy ne h₁ésti bʰéh₂mi-kʷe. gʰósteyes me ḱlush₁yónti litént-kʷe. ne kʷis me gʷr̥néHti. ǵérh₂onts pérdt.
examples.en: I am born from an old man. I have no mouth, and I speak. The guests hear me and go away. No one praises me. The old man has farted.

examples.pie: ǵérh₂onts pérkʷunom dh₂pnóy gʷr̥néHt. nu pérdt. h₂yuHn̥ḱṓs sméyn̥t. ǵérh₂onts sokʷéyet. mē sméyte. pérkʷunos gʰrémet. ḱléwt me. nu h₂yuHn̥ḱṓs pérkʷunom gʷr̥nHént.
examples.en: At the sacrificial feast an elder was praising Perkʷunos. Then he farted loudly. The young men laughed. The elder said: "Do not laugh!" "Perkʷunos rumbled." "He heard me." Then the young men praised Perkʷunos.

examples.pie: wódr̥ pérwr̥ h₂n̥réh₁ ne térdt. h₂yúh₁ térdt. sruméns h₁ukdʰí.
examples.en: Water does not bore the rock by force. By long time it bores through. Learn from the stream.

examples.pie: pérkʷum h₂isḱé. h₁ím tm̥h₁dʰí. kʷékʷlom h₁ésmōd piḱdʰí. h₁ím h₁óloh₁ tr̥ddʰí. h₁yód kʷékʷlos Hrunépetor mē HréwdHs. kʷékʷlom h₂ew wr̥ǵdʰí. h₁yós ne Hrumptór só méh₂trey lewbʰós h₁ésti.
examples.en: Seek an oak. Cut it. Carve a wheel out of it. Bore through it with the awl. If the wheel breaks, do not cry out. Make the wheel again. Whichever does not break, that one is dear to the mother.

examples.pie: wiHrós swóm gʷéru Hyéh₁kt h₁íd-kʷe Hrumptó. dʰénh₂t wĺ̥kʷos h₁ím próti. wiHrós bʰéyh₂t. h₁ésyo bʰréh₂tēr ǵʰoysóm h₁épt. ǵʰoysós h₁ésyo ḱḗr térdt. mért wĺ̥kʷos. nu bʰréh₂tēr wiHrṓy gʷéru wérǵt.
examples.en: The man threw his own spear, and it broke. The wolf set off running at him. The man became afraid. His brother seized the javelin. The javelin pierced its heart. The wolf died. Then the brother made a spear for the man.

examples.pie: gʰrómosyo deywós HeHḱúns h₁éḱwons h₂éǵet. gʰrómos yéh₂t n̥bʰrós-kʷe tóm sékʷeto. tósyo kʷékʷlōs kʷl̥h₁ént. h₁ógʷʰis tóm kʷéḱt. nu só trémt só-kʷe ní sérpet. gʷʰént h₁ógʷʰim. wédōr térkh₂t. nu só h₂epó léytt.
examples.en: The god of thunder drove swift horses. Thunder went, and the rain-cloud followed him. His wheels turned. Then the serpent saw him, and trembled, and crept down. He slew the serpent. He released the waters. Then he went away.

examples.pie: gʷr̥Hḗi h₂ówis, kʷésyo wlh₂néH ne (h₁é) est, h₁éḱwons spéḱet, h₁oinom gʰe gʷr̥Húm wóǵʰom wéǵʰontm̥ h₁oinom-kʷe méǵHm bʰórom, h₁oinom-kʷe ǵʰménm̥ Hṓḱu bʰérontm̥.
examples.en: A sheep that had no wool saw horses, one of them pulling a heavy wagon, one carrying a big load, and one carrying a man quickly.

examples.pie: dʰubʰnóm bʰréh₁wr̥ bʰeh₂nóm wédos wéǵʰeti. kr̥snós-kʷe spḗr tód píph₃eti.
examples.en: The deep spring carries the shiny water. And the black sparrow drinks it.

examples.pie: kʷíd wóǵʰosyo bʰórom bʰéreti? wéǵʰeti kʷékʷlos tóm.
examples.en: What carries the burden of the wagon? The wheel transports it.

examples.pie: dn̥ǵʰwéh₂m me toy doḱéye. wékʷesh₂ moy ḱléwse h₁íh₂-kʷe wérh₁ye. ḱód wódr̥. ḱód péh₂wr̥. h₁éwkm̥.
examples.en: Teach me your tongue! Listen to my words and say them! This is water. This is fire. I have learned!

examples.pie: kʷíd só wérh₁yeti? só wékʷos wérh₁yeti.
examples.en: What does he say? He says a word.

examples.pie: dʰéh₁mn̥ wérh₁yet ḱl̥nwént-kʷe tóy.
examples.en: He was saying the ordinance, and they listened.

examples.pie: h₁sónt ḱuh₁róm ne-kʷe mért dʰrówgʰos ml̥dús. h₁yós dʰrugʰyéti só bʰéh₂esos bʰebʰóyh₂e. dʰrówgʰosyo pódh₁e mr̥ǵʰúh₁.
examples.en: The truth is strong, and it does not die; the lie is weak. He who deceives fears the light. The feet of a lie are short.

examples.pie: nu moy h₂éwsos suHnúm dh₃dʰí. ḱuh₁rós ǵn̥h₃rós ḱlutós-kʷe h₁syéh₁t. h₁ésyo-kʷe ḱléwos méǵh₂ h₁syéh₁t. nu tébʰye sweh₂dú médʰu ǵʰḗm.
examples.en: Now, Dawn, give me a son! May he be strong and wise and famous. And may his fame be great. Now I have poured the sweet mead for you.

examples.pie: h₁éḱwōs sn̥h₂énti? h₁éḱwōs sn̥h₂énti h₂ékʷeh₂s-kʷe ne bʰebʰih₂ḗr. nu moy déh₂nu h₁éḱwoh₁ ḱóm péroh₂. h₁ím wédni mē séh₁s. srówos ḱuh₁rós.
examples.en: Do horses swim? Horses swim, and they do not fear the water. Then I will cross the river with my horse. Do not let go of him in the water. The current is strong.

examples.pie: ph₂ter moy ǵʰóstos dʰégʷʰeti. kʷíd dʰéh₁s? kʷérom h₁épm̥ gʷʰermós-kʷe h₁ést. ǵʰóstom toy h₂ékʷeh₂i logʰéye. kʷéros h₂éydʰoy h₁épi gʷʰermós. nu moy ǵʰóstos ne dʰégʷʰeti. h₁ím skuHtíh₁ h₁pdʰí.
examples.en: Father, my hand is burning! What did you do? I seized the pot, and it was hot. Lay your hand in the water. A pot on the fire is hot. Now my hand is not burning. Seize it with a skin.

examples.pie: kʷŕ̥mey h₁éǵʰs h₁néwn̥ wr̥míbʰis ḱóm gʷh₂dʰí. kʷŕ̥mey snéh₁wōr mosgʰṓd ih₂dʰí. wórmey mḗms sn̥h₁wénbʰos h₁idʰí. nu skéwHtim mémsos sérpe. kʷŕ̥mey soksóm skuHtéys litdʰí. nu kʷŕ̥mey h₂én mr̥dʰí h₂éti-kʷe mē gʷéms.
examples.en: Go out, worm, with nine worms! Go, worm, from the marrow into the sinews! Go, worm, from the sinews into the flesh! Now crawl from the flesh into the skin! Go away, worm, from the skin into the stone! Now die there, worm, and do not come back!

examples.pie: h₂éti gʷegʷómth₂e. kʷíd moréyes? h₂ŕ̥tḱom. bʰréh₂teres moy h₁ím dṓm bʰéronti. h₂ŕ̥tḱos sph₁rós. h₁ésyo nos skéwHtis ǵʰyémi stégeti h₁ésyo-kʷe sélpos tinh₁més. h₂ŕ̥tḱos te ne dénḱt? skélos moy dénḱt kéh₂ilos h₁ésmi.
examples.en: You have come back! What did you kill? A bear. My brothers are carrying it home. The bear is fat! Its skin will cover us in winter, and we will melt its fat. Did the bear not bite you? It bit my leg, but I am whole.

examples.pie: wéh₁ikom h₂usési gʷh₂dʰí. nu sddʰí h₂ówins ḱóm. úd mē HréwdHs. tā́s mē stunéds. téh₂bʰos bʰh₂dʰí. tā́s h₂ml̥ǵdʰí. bʰére bʰórom h₁n̥dóm.
examples.en: At dawn go to the enclosure. Sit down beside the sheep. Do not cry out. Do not hit them. Speak to them. Milk them. Carry the load inside.

examples.pie: bʰuHyét nébʰos h₂wérst-kʷe. nu h₂óweyes trésont. h₂nḗr tā́s wéh₁ikom wédʰet. h₁éyt moysós pró téh₂es-kʷe sékʷonto. nu dʰwóri sédt. nu tód h₂wést h₁n̥dʰént-kʷe h₁éǵʰs.
examples.en: A cloud was appearing, and it rained. The sheep trembled in fear. The man led them into the enclosure. The ram went ahead, and they followed. Then he sat down at the door. Then it grew bright, and they came out.

examples.pie: h₁yód h₁regʷesyét sérpet wĺ̥kʷos wéh₁ikom. h₂éǵmn̥ tréset. ḱwṓ tóm ḱléwt só-kʷe HréwdHt. nu bʰéwdʰt h₂nḗr. nu swóm gʷéru h₁pónts só wĺ̥kʷom dʰwóri kʷéḱt. nu tóm tóh₁ moréyet. nu só h₂ew légʰt.
examples.en: When it was getting dark, the wolf crept toward the enclosure. The flock trembled in fear. The dog heard it, and he cried out. Then the man woke up. Seizing his spear, he caught sight of the wolf at the door. Then he killed it. Then he lay down again.

examples.pie: h₁nómn̥ toy newowékʷos? h₁íd newowékʷos. mórtōs h₁íd sénoybʰos wékʷesbʰos tétḱn̥t. séneh₂ wékʷesh₂ h₁wésuh₂. h₁íh₂ méǵʰye priHéh₂.
examples.en: Is your name a new word? It is a new word. Mortals made it from old words. Old words are good. They are dear to me.

source.name: coinage
source.note: Determinative 'new-word' (néwos 'new' + wékʷos 'word'): 'neologism' is Gk νέος 'new' + λόγος 'word' (+ -ism).

source.name: coinage
source.note: dóru 'tree' in the sense 'wood, forest' that the tree word has in the west: OIr. fid 'tree; wood; forest' and PGmc *widu- 'tree; wood' (Kroonen 2013 s.v. *widu-; Matasović 2009 s.v. *widu-), E wood. The inherited *(h₁)widʰ-u- itself (h₁widʰh₁us) has no sourced accent and no engine spec, so it cannot be offered.
